title: Looking for character in MV style based on hospital mascot

posts.author: mrcookie
posts.body:
My friends and I are making a game for our friend to play at his Extra Life charity fundraising marathon (any commercial distribution of the game would only be sold as a fundraiser with all proceeds to charity, if it's ever released - we would ask that you let us use it for this purpose). Since it's just for charity, we'll be using mostly MV RTP including the default generated characters / art style.
We were hoping to incorporate our local children's hospital mascot ("Dr. Goodbear") as a playable character since we're raising money for our hospital, if we can get assets that don't look totally out of place:
Maker Format:
MV
Makers I Own:
MV
Art Style:
MV RTP
Description of Request:
1. Character Face
- Hoping for a few basic expressions that we can use for dialogue interactions (happy/default, sad, frown kind of thing)
- Would really like to match the MV art style to keep a consistent feel with the default characters we'll be generating
2. Sprites
- Need the walking/damage/battler sprite image files that would be generated by the character generator, as this character will be a full party member
Description of Dr. Goodbear:
A bear mascot that wears a teal t-shirt, no pants. Typically shown wearing either a stethoscope or a hospital ID badge. He stands upright and walks on two legs. He won't have a weapon like a sword in our game - he's a bear, so will do claw damage and take swipes for physical attacks. Attack animation could be related to swiping/punching or something else suitable.
Reference Images:
-
https://www.rrc.ca/academic-news/wp-content/uploads/sites/90/2023/04/Dr.-Goodbear-2-768x1024.jpg
-
https://goodbear.ca/dq-raises-funds-for-kids-across-canada-on-miracletreatday/
(mascot photo in the article, plus you can also see the cartoon logo representation at the top left of the page)
Thank you in advance for your consideration!

posts.author: Avery
posts.body:
You might not be aware of it, but you are really asking for a lot here. That is at least a full day of work for an experienced artist to do for all the components.
So you will either have to hope someone is really really invested in your project or have to tailor your expectations a little.
For example, I actually have a walking teddy bear that would probably work if you tweaked the color of his shirt, but due to it being an edit of the default MZ tileset teddy, you need to own RMMZ as well to be allowed to use it. (Full terms of use are in the download)

posts.body:
Hey, thanks for this! It's good to know that it's quite a big ask as I don't have the experience to know. I did stumble across ColaLime's bear as a backup, he just looks so mean but we can only do what we can do.
However in a twist, apparently now one of our friends is potentially interested in finding out what it would cost to pitch in and actually get this character made. Is the classifieds area here the best place to go about finding someone who can work on this?

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
mrcookie said:
Is the classifieds area here the best place to go about finding someone who can work on this?
Click to expand...
I wouldn't say "the best place" but it's definitely a strong option.
However, in order to prevent spam and marketing, the classifieds section is not available to anyone with less than 30 posts.
You can search any art hosting website for pixel artists and try reaching out to them to see if they would be interested in being commissioned.
Although I originally began my search for my own pixel artist here, in the end I found my pixel artist on Pixiv.
Be sure to contact a few people, not everyone is available. So don't get your mind set on any one artist, but keep an eye out for many possible artists, and contact them all. The worst they can say is "No."
When contacting pixel artists outside of RPG Maker, they may not be familiar with the asset standards, so make sure you know how to properly format the sprite sheets so you can tell them how to format it.
Assuming you watermark any RTP ( to prevent distribution of assets, if they do not own RPG maker), you can also send them some of the existing character sheets so they have a template format to follow.
Good luck.
